subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should classic voice calls gain a provider-generic streaming telephony contract now, and which provider/transport combinations must the first implementation support?
rationale: Current generic speech streaming is insufficient for telephony framing and sample-rate conversion, so implementation requires a public plugin API choice plus explicit fallback and transport scope rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Generic contract, Twilio first
options.body: Add the public telephony stream seam and prove it with Twilio plus at least one capable speech provider, then add Telnyx through the same contract.

options.title: Require Twilio and Telnyx
options.body: Hold implementation until both transports can land together with equivalent ordering, abort, and fallback proof.

options.title: Keep classic calls buffered
options.body: Decline the new contract and direct latency-sensitive deployments to the separate full-duplex realtime voice mode.

recommendation.title: Generic contract, Twilio first
recommendation.body: Add the public telephony stream seam and prove it with Twilio plus at least one capable speech provider, then add Telnyx through the same contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sustained history across the affected response, TTS, transport, realtime, configuration, and documentation surfaces.
